title: SRS strategic map
purpose: A map of the capabilities and release boundaries needed for semantic sovereignty and practical human–AI collaboration.
bootstrapStatus: This map is a curated logical SRS projection: stable strategic entities, explicit semantic links, and separate assessments. It will later materialize as SRS Records, Relations, Containers and DocumentViews after the post-#256 model settles.

mission.decisionAuthority: The project owner is currently the sole decision-maker.
mission.purpose: Increase collective agency by helping groups develop the practice of making clear, accountable decisions together in an age of AI.
mission.muDemocracy: muDemocracy turns ordinary conversation into a living practice of collective decision-making. AI makes skilled facilitation and coaching more accessible; judgment, commitment and authority remain with people.
mission.srs: SRS is an open standard for portable semantic documents that people and AI can understand and use. Semantic sovereignty means a group can possess, inspect, understand, move, present and continue working with its meaning without dependence on the application, service, storage provider or AI model that created it.
mission.humanAiConstitution: AI may observe, extract, propose, question, organise, explain and coach. People decide, agree, ratify and remain accountable.
roadmapTests: Does it help a group practise and improve collective decision-making?
Does it complete the meeting-to-ratified-record loop?
Does it make meaning independently understandable and navigable?
Does it preserve meaning across tools, storage systems, AI providers and time?
Does it keep AI assistive and human authority explicit?
Does it establish or protect a root invariant that becomes expensive to change after release?

applicationStrategy.name: srs-web / app.mudemocracy.org
applicationStrategy.role: The first usable SRS application: an opinionated surface for people to inspect, edit, validate and work with their own semantic repositories.
applicationStrategy.architecture: One repository runtime and one canonical edit, save, import and export path. Repository, container workspace, facilitation and blueprint-authoring modes are projections over that shared substrate, never separate semantic stores.
boundaries: The application is generic about repository, Record, Relation, Container, Package, validation, navigation and preservation behaviour.
Blueprints select a workspace and presentation without changing canonical meaning.
Governance packages define decisions, roles, ratification, review and supersession; they are replaceable application content, not application-owned semantics.
Protocols guide work against canonical state; DocumentViews present it; neither becomes an authoritative store.
AI proposes visibly within a current Protocol or Blueprint context. Human review and ratification alone commit canonical meaning.

modes.name: Repository inspection and direct semantic editing
Container workspace for ordinary group work

applicationStrategy.predecessor: The separate decision-logger repository is an earlier prototype and research corpus. It informs fixtures, scenarios and migration learning, but is not a canonical SRS producer, consumer or release dependency unless explicitly restarted on current SRS contracts.

reality.method: This is an assessed evidence snapshot, not an issue-status calculation. A claim is proven only by a runnable surface, repeatable test, walkthrough or durable artifact; partial means a useful fragment exists but the boundary promise is not yet demonstrated.

capabilityArchitecture.purpose: The standard-level contracts that make the release boundaries and practice paths possible. A contract is not an application feature: it is a promise that independent SRS implementations can rely on.

stability.label: Lock before F1
stability.meaning: A root semantic contract. Changing it after the coherent-kernel release would require a breaking migration.

stability.label: Settle before F2
stability.meaning: Required for an independently understandable, portable SRS publication.

stability.label: Settle before F3
stability.meaning: Required when a repository can be continued and reconciled across installations.

stability.label: Extension or profile
stability.meaning: Built on the stable substrate; it may evolve without redefining the preservation kernel.

stability.label: Deliberately deferred
stability.meaning: Important, but not required for the current public SRS boundary.

capabilityPipelines.name: Governance practice
capabilityPipelines.purpose: A group adopts only the semantic and procedural structure its practice needs next. These stages describe a capability path, not a release plan or issue hierarchy.

stages.name: Simple decision log
stages.groupNeed: We need a small shared form that lets us remember what we decided.
stages.promise: A group records decisions with the four-field Quick Log blueprint while retaining a capable canonical Decision Record beneath it.
semanticAdds: explicit absent rather than inferred information
stages.activationTrigger: A group wants to record and read back decisions without adopting a governance process.

stages.name: Living decisions
stages.groupNeed: We need to share a draft, return to it, revisit commitments and replace a decision without losing its history.
stages.promise: A Decision Record has stable identity through drafting, review, revisit and supersession; operational version history may remain in Git until interoperable history exchange is needed.
doesNotIntroduce: a new semantic Record for every working edit
stages.activationTrigger: A group needs decisions to remain useful after the meeting in which they first appeared.

stages.name: Accountable decisions
stages.groupNeed: We need to say when a decision was made, who participated and whether the group actually ratified it.
stages.promise: A decision can be refined across several sessions and linked to declared participation and ratification without making any session the owner of the decision.
stages.activationTrigger: A group needs the participation, timing or authority of a decision to be inspectable.

stages.name: Delegated practice
stages.groupNeed: We need working groups or roles, and need to make their mandates and authority legible.
stages.promise: A group can define roles, working groups and mandates, then connect decisions to the authority under which they were made.
stages.activationTrigger: A group delegates recurring work or needs to distinguish who may decide what.

stages.name: Constituted group
stages.groupNeed: We need to maintain our purpose, objectives and foundational rules, including how those rules may change.
stages.promise: A group maintains purpose and founding documents as governed Records with explicit amendment and special-ratification policy rather than immutable application configuration.
stages.activationTrigger: A group needs a durable shared purpose or a rule for changing its own rules.

stages.name: Facilitated practice
stages.groupNeed: We want to make a decision together in the room or online, one clear step at a time.
stages.promise: A shared-screen Protocol guides people through canonical decision state, can resume after interruption, and ends in whole-record review and human ratification.
stages.activationTrigger: A group wants help holding an actual shared decision process, not merely editing a record.

stages.name: AI-assisted practice
stages.groupNeed: We want AI to propose useful wording and coaching from conversation evidence while people retain judgment and authority.
stages.promise: AI works inside a current Protocol or Blueprint context, proposes visibly with provenance, and never commits canonical meaning without human review and ratification.
stages.activationTrigger: A group has a reliable manual Protocol practice and wants assistive coaching or transcript-grounded drafting.

capabilityPipelines.name: Semantic document practice
capabilityPipelines.purpose: A group defines and maintains the meaning, structure and publication facets of a real document together. These are adoption capabilities, not a CMS feature tree or a second set of release gates.

stages.name: Structured semantic document
stages.groupNeed: We need to write a guide, policy, specification or handbook without separating its content from the structure that makes it understandable.
stages.promise: A document is authored as typed Records in a Container, with explicit fields and relations instead of an opaque page blob.
stages.activationTrigger: A group needs a document whose structure and meaning must remain inspectable as it is written.

research.takeaway: Content is maintained meaning: fields need an inspectable change history, not a monolithic document blob.

stages.name: Composed semantic document
stages.groupNeed: We need documents with repeatable structure and reusable concepts, rather than one-off forms for every guide or policy.
stages.promise: Blueprints, type inheritance, shared Fields and package definitions compose validated multi-record documents without making the editor own the ontology.
stages.activationTrigger: A group repeats document patterns and wants structure to be reusable, reviewable and independently understandable.

research.takeaway: A reusable document library distributes its definitions, Views, DocumentViews, Protocols and Themes as one explicit package closure.

stages.name: Faceted publication
stages.groupNeed: We need to read, edit, print and publish the same document differently without duplicating or losing its meaning.
stages.promise: Authoring, reading, generic fallback and website or print publication are explicit facets over canonical meaning; a publication adapter never becomes the only reader.
doesNotIntroduce: a single View for editing and publication
a required theme or website runtime
stages.activationTrigger: A document must serve readers in more than one context while remaining recoverable without its preferred presentation.

research.takeaway: A conforming reader needs a normative baseline when no View is available.
Authoring and publication Views have incompatible purposes and must remain separate projections.

stages.name: Living document library
stages.groupNeed: We need to revise content, evolve document definitions and reuse shared pieces without obscuring what changed or breaking existing documents.
stages.promise: Document content and definitions evolve through visible revision, migration and compatibility practices; reusable content remains linked to its semantic context.
stages.activationTrigger: A group maintains a document library long enough that shared definitions and previously published content must change safely.

research.takeaway: Revision chains make individual semantic changes auditable and safely restorable.

stages.name: Portable semantic publication
stages.groupNeed: We need another person or tool to take a document, its definitions and its readable meaning elsewhere without depending on our website or editor.
stages.promise: A publication carries the definition closure, canonical Records and Relations, provenance/completeness diagnostics and a generic readable facet; a later user can continue it without silent loss.
doesNotIntroduce: a promise that every attachment is included without a declaration
stages.activationTrigger: A document must remain usable and explainable after leaving the system that authored or published it.

research.takeaway: Portable subsets need explicit identity, closure, provenance-completeness and import semantics rather than a bespoke export format.

tracks.name: Sovereignty
tracks.purpose: Meaning survives independently of the system that created it.

tracks.name: Decision practice
tracks.purpose: Groups create, maintain and improve accountable decisions together.

boundaries.name: Coherent Semantic Kernel
boundaries.actor: Maintainer of a first-party SRS package
boundaries.promise: One authoritative semantic model migrates and regenerates without silent meaning loss.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Migrated first-party corpus with generated conformance evidence.
boundaries.walkthrough: Regenerate the first-party corpus from the authoritative model, validate it through independent Node and Rust paths, and inspect canonical state through more than one DocumentView.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: The migrated kernel has one source of truth and reproducible projections.
boundaries.stableAfter: Core identity, reference resolution and regeneration invariants are stable enough to build outward.

boundaries.name: Meaning You Can Take / SRS 2.0
boundaries.actor: Independent user with no originating-service access
boundaries.promise: A realistic SRS governance repository opens, validates, explains itself and renders offline as a self-contained semantic repository.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Portable `.srs` export, generic readable fallback and independent conformance proof.
entryCriteria: Archive, completeness and version-closure tests are defined
boundaries.walkthrough: Export an SRS-native governance repository or fixed governance fixture, disconnect from its originating service, then recover definitions, records, relations, provenance and a readable facet while accurately reporting missing evidence or unsupported semantics.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: Frozen publications resolve their declared closure reproducibly and remain independent of live Views.
boundaries.stableAfter: The public SRS boundary: Continuity becomes the default.

gaps.title: SRS-web F2 portable-reader walkthrough
gaps.trigger: Create and make a gate when the SRS-web repository runtime can open a portable archive without service access.

boundaries.name: Meaning You Can Continue Elsewhere
boundaries.actor: Collaborator continuing work from a clone or export
boundaries.promise: A user edits offline, inspects semantic differences and reintegrates without losing identity, relations, provenance or unsupported content.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Reintegrated repository with reviewable semantic diff and preserved unsupported-content diagnostics.
entryCriteria: Diff and reintegration contracts are accepted
boundaries.walkthrough: Clone or export a repository, make an offline change, inspect the semantic diff, and reintegrate while verifying record identities, relations, provenance and opaque extensions.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: Interchange never silently discards data a conforming reader cannot interpret.
boundaries.stableAfter: Offline continuation and reintegration form a reliable cross-installation collaboration boundary.

boundaries.name: Living Decisions
boundaries.actor: Group returning to its decisions over time
boundaries.promise: A group uses the SRS-web governance workspace to review commitments when due and supersede decisions with an accountable history.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Upgradable decision repository with living-decision history.
boundaries.walkthrough: In srs-web, upgrade a repository, identify a decision due for review, supersede it, and inspect the resulting history.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: Package upgrades and supersession preserve prior decision meaning and lineage.
boundaries.stableAfter: The SRS-web governance workspace supports decisions as a maintained practice, not a one-time log.

boundaries.name: Facilitated Decisions
boundaries.actor: Group using the shared-screen facilitation mode of the SRS-web governance workspace
boundaries.promise: A group works through a projected semantic Protocol, agrees wording live and ratifies a complete decision.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Ratified decision produced by a resumable Protocol run and readable as a whole.
entryCriteria: SRS-web can open and edit the governance container workspace
boundaries.walkthrough: In the same SRS-web repository workspace, project a Protocol, guide the group through each stage, resume after interruption, review the assembled record, ratify it and later read it back.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: The Protocol presents and guides canonical meaning; it does not own or alter it.
boundaries.stableAfter: Shared-screen manual facilitation is a first-class SRS-web mode, not a separate editor.

gaps.title: P2/P3 substrate split in existing story bodies
gaps.trigger: Before P2 implementation, move TSS emission and transcript-linked provenance from the manual P2 contract into P3 while retaining Protocol-run attention state in P2.

boundaries.name: AI-Assisted Decisions
boundaries.actor: Group using AI inside the current SRS-web Protocol workspace
boundaries.promise: AI reads a live or recorded transcript, proposes stage-appropriate text with provenance, and people edit, agree and ratify it.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Human-ratified decision with transcript-linked AI proposal provenance.
entryCriteria: Addressability and Protocol runs are available
exclusions: A separate AI-specific editor or canonical store
boundaries.walkthrough: In the same SRS-web Protocol workspace, use a live transcript, request a stage recommendation, edit it with the group, ratify the resulting decision and inspect the source provenance.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: AI assistance never silently commits canonical meaning; attribution and human ratification remain inspectable.
boundaries.stableAfter: AI may participate as a transparent coach inside a human-owned decision practice.

gaps.title: TSS schema and transcript-ingestion contract
gaps.trigger: Create concrete stories after P2 establishes the manual Protocol run.

gaps.title: AI-assisted meeting walkthrough
gaps.trigger: Create when transcript ingestion and stage recommendations have runnable surfaces.

standardContracts.name: Coherent semantic kernel
standardContracts.promise: Independent implementations resolve the same canonical meaning, validate it consistently, and regenerate reproducible projections.
notIncluded: A particular editor, database, governance model or preferred layout

standardContracts.name: Identity and reference resolution
standardContracts.promise: Records, definitions and structural members have durable identity and unambiguous references across a repository and its installed packages.
notIncluded: Repository-copy and merge identity

standardContracts.name: Definitions and structural navigation
standardContracts.promise: Fields, Types, Records, Relations, Containers and Packages compose inspectable semantic documents with navigable structure.
notIncluded: Website-specific document or decision schemas

standardContracts.name: Layered default values
standardContracts.promise: When a real authoring surface needs pre-filled values, it can use one versioned layered-default mechanism whose effective value resolves Protocol → Type → Field; a default never satisfies a required Field.
notIncluded: A separate default mechanism at each of the Field, Type and Protocol layers
Treating a default as satisfying requiredness
A current F1, F2, F3 or practice-track release gate

standardContracts.name: Canonical meaning and facets
standardContracts.promise: A repository declares one repository-owned set of presentations it commits to render and can produce reproducible, readable projections from canonical meaning; neither the presentations nor their projections becomes an authoritative store.
notIncluded: A single required renderer, theme or layout-preservation promise
Byte-identical rendering across independent implementations

standardContracts.name: Portable semantic publication
standardContracts.promise: A person can take an SRS repository away from its originating service and still recover its definitions, canonical meaning, provenance and a readable orientation.
notIncluded: Editing, merge, federation or a promise that every attachment is present

standardContracts.name: Definition closure and completeness
standardContracts.promise: A frozen publication declares the exact definitions and versions it needs, and accurately reports evidence or other content that is absent.
notIncluded: Silent substitution of live definitions or implied evidence completeness

standardContracts.name: Generic orientation and fallback rendering
standardContracts.promise: A conforming reader can navigate and explain a repository without its preferred application, theme or DocumentView.
notIncluded: Reproducing a publisher’s exact visual layout

standardContracts.name: Continuation and reconciliation
standardContracts.promise: A repository can be copied, changed elsewhere and reconciled without silently losing semantic identity, relations, provenance or unsupported content.
notIncluded: Hosted VCS, federation negotiation or automatic conflict resolution

standardContracts.name: Copy identity, semantic diff and merge
standardContracts.promise: Independent implementations can compare and reintegrate semantic changes using stable identity and explicit conflict semantics rather than raw-file coincidence.
notIncluded: A required storage backend or a guarantee that every conflict is automatically resolved

standardContracts.name: Practice extensions
standardContracts.promise: Governance and collaboration practices use the preservation substrate, but do not redefine it.
notIncluded: A universal governance ontology or mandatory AI behaviour

standardContracts.name: Governance profile
standardContracts.promise: Decision, role, mandate, ratification and founding-document semantics are installable domain definitions, not SRS root types.
notIncluded: Hard-coded governance behaviour in a generic reader

standardContracts.name: Protocol and AI provenance
standardContracts.promise: A Protocol can guide a human process, while transcript-linked AI proposals carry inspectable provenance and human ratification evidence.
notIncluded: AI authority to commit canonical meaning

standardContracts.name: Integrity profiles and federation
standardContracts.promise: Cryptographic authority, attestations and cross-community semantic negotiation remain future layers above portable meaning.
notIncluded: A requirement for the F1, F2 or F3 release promises

standardContracts.name: Addressability and attention state
standardContracts.promise: Tools can identify semantic locations and preserve a live point of attention.
notIncluded: A required Git, database or archive backend
AI authority to commit canonical meaning

standardContracts.name: Attribution mechanism (relation provenance)
standardContracts.promise: When a real consumer needs who/when/why on a relation or assertion, one single-shaped attribution mechanism — one asserter vocabulary, one timestamp convention, one reference-to-source convention — expresses it; attribution is always optional and never overrides the record, and can only be promoted into office by a verification mechanism (a signature, a ratified decision, a verified publisher).
notIncluded: The removed five-shape provenance machinery (assertedBy, confidence, status, createdBy, validFrom, validUntil on Relation)
Attribution as a requirement for validity
standardContracts.returnTrigger: The return claimant arrives: travelling packages need trustable publishers, or agent-written content needs marking. The mechanism then designed must satisfy all three clauses.

standardContracts.name: Federation (registry, events, cross-repository relations)
standardContracts.promise: Federation is core to SRS and returns as a planned roadmap phase — grounded in the sharing forms that actually emerged (bundles, slices, git-hosted repositories) and the axis 4-10 verification path; the removal is a deliberate reset of a design that predated real practice, not a judgment on the capability. Sits beside the integrity-and-federation contract, which covers the cryptographic-authority and negotiation layer above it.
notIncluded: The removed federation registry, federation events, and cross-repository relation fields
Cryptographic authority or cross-community semantic negotiation (see integrity-and-federation)
standardContracts.returnTrigger: federation is core to SRS (owner, 2026-08-22); this removal is a deliberate reset of a design that predates real practice, not a judgment on the capability. The redesign returns as a planned roadmap phase, grounded in the sharing forms that actually emerged (bundles, slices, git-hosted repositories) and the axis 4-10 verification path; the owner schedules it.

standardContracts.name: Revisions and Changelog (field-level transition history)
standardContracts.promise: When a consumer needs transition history or field-level audit, a history mechanism is designed against its actual requirements. Record state (lifecycleState, the canonical case) mutates in place under the machine-bound state carve-out; semantic content still changes only by version increment or successor-and-link.
notIncluded: The removed per-field Revision sidecars (revisions.json) and ChangelogCollection (changelog.json)
The revision-dependent clauses of ext:addressability's lifecycle coupling
standardContracts.returnTrigger: The roadmap return trigger: a consumer needs transition history or field-level audit - anticipated first claimant is the muDemocracy Decision Log governance audit surface. Also review if a second field class beyond lifecycleState claims the state carve-out; the machine-bound test must hold or the boundary is wrong.

standardContracts.name: Tier 1 (TypedRecord middle rung)
standardContracts.promise: If a real consumer produces semi-structured records — named fields, no Type — that fit neither a Note's free-text sections nor a lightweight Type, the middle tier returns as an evidence-shaped design, not the removed one. Until then the record model stands at two tiers (Note, Record); graduation is expressed as Note-to-Record via derived-from.
notIncluded: The removed TypedRecord entity and its graduatedAt timestamp
Tier 1 in the discovery Text Projection or the tier taxonomy prose
standardContracts.returnTrigger: The roadmap return trigger: a real consumer produces semi-structured records (named fields, no Type) that fit neither Note sections nor a lightweight Type. Until then, the two-tier model stands.

standardContracts.name: ext:repeatable-fields
standardContracts.promise: If a consumer emerges with genuine array-valued Field assignments, repeatable fields return — as a merge with RFC-032 cardinality's existing list semantics, not necessarily a revival of the removed mechanism.
notIncluded: The removed ext:repeatable-fields extension outside a stale ancestor tree
standardContracts.returnTrigger: a consumer with genuine array-valued assignments (note: RFC-032 cardinality already carries list semantics - the return may be a merge, not a revival).

standardContracts.name: SectionSource fixed-instances and relation-query variants
standardContracts.promise: If a document composition need arises that neither of the two live SectionSource kinds (container-subset, type-query) expresses, a variant returns designed against that need; one way over many holds until then.
notIncluded: The removed SectionSource fixed-instances and relation-query variants
standardContracts.returnTrigger: a composition need neither live variant expresses.

standardContracts.name: View.protection (view-root edit-protection enum)
standardContracts.promise: If a real authoring surface needs edit protection, the missing enforcement half is designed then; a hint without a contract (none/read-only/fill-in with no enforcement semantics defined anywhere) is not restored as-is.
notIncluded: The removed View.protection enum (corrected attribution: it sat on the View, not on FieldView)
FieldView.required, which is unaffected — attested in production use and dispositioned separately
standardContracts.returnTrigger: a real authoring surface needing edit protection, which must design the missing enforcement half.

standardContracts.name: KEYED reference alias resolution
standardContracts.promise: Alias resolution returns only with practice-sharing evidence. Until then, KEYED references are key-only (one name over many); renaming a substrate entry is a supersession act through the status vocabulary.
notIncluded: Alias resolution for KEYED references
A second resolution path alongside the declared reference strengths
standardContracts.returnTrigger: returns via the roadmap only with practice-sharing evidence.
